recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-16028 unless Patient Care opens a new issue to reverse FHIR-24684 and restore a dedicated detector element.
issue_request: FHIR-16028 was a Published Patient Care / Persuasive change request asking to add AdverseEvent.detector 0..* Reference(Patient | RelatedPerson | Practitioner | PractitionerRole | Device), defined as who or what identified a change in physiological state or condition.
initial_application: The Jira-comment-linked commit 5bf6a7e41755de3d973ffda0787a868d3123a6d1 applied the request in the old AdverseEvent spreadsheet by adding AdverseEvent.detector.
additional_context: FHIR-24684 later reached Published / Not Persuasive with Modification and resolved to remove detector, add AUT to the AdverseEvent participant-function value set, and leave detected unrenamed because detector was folded into participant. The combined branch already contains FHIR-24684 audit commit 919573a8205d9fea04191414ef3a4a6229e28008.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current build-scope source defines AdverseEvent.participant, participant.function, and participant.actor; the participant-function value set includes AUT; and an exact current-source search found no AdverseEvent.detector or asserter/assertedDate residue.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Patient Care decision removed AdverseEvent.detector and folded that role into participant; it is already audited on the combined branch.
